card.title: Why video calls skip the resend

body.claim: TCP resends lost data to make delivery reliable, while UDP does not, which suits real-time uses like voice calls and games.
body.why: TCP sets up a connection with a three-way handshake, retransmits lost packets and keeps data in order, which adds delay. UDP has no handshake and no guarantee of delivery or ordering, but its lack of retransmission delays suits real-time applications such as voice over IP and online games.

probes.question: Why does UDP suit real-time applications like voice calls?

Ordered data transfer: the destination host rearranges segments according to a sequence number
